threshold_rationale: Round, common minimum for a per-class F1 estimate to be minimally statistically meaningful; also exactly matches the boundary Phase 1 inspection already reports (classes_below_50_support), so no new threshold was invented specifically for this policy.
rare_class_treatment_detail: Rare classes are NEVER excluded from the dataset, never dropped from train/val/test splits, and never merged into an Other bucket -- the full 21-component taxonomy is preserved everywhere. They are excluded only from the denominator of the PRIMARY headline macro-F1 figure (examples whose true label is a rare class do not contribute to that unweighted per-class average), because a single class with 15 total examples produces a per-class F1 estimate too noisy to usefully average alongside classes with thousands of examples. They remain fully visible via: (1) full micro-F1, computed over ALL examples including rare ones, naturally weighted by true frequency; (2) a dedicated rare-class secondary report (precision/recall/F1/support per rare class, from the exact same predictions used everywhere else); (3) the confusion matrix, which always includes every class.

orthogonal_axes.primary_vs_rare: this policy -- based on total dataset class support
orthogonal_axes.stable_label_slice: a SEPARATE axis (issues with zero recorded Component-change events, 82.2% of Platform issues per reports/phase1_platform.json) applied independently -- the primary/rare split is evaluated both on the full test set and, secondarily, on the stable-label subset; the two axes are never conflated into one category.
